_README: Numerosity Exp1 configuration. Every tunable of the task lives here; code contains no task numbers. Keys starting with '_' are comments and are ignored by the loader. Paths in '_pilot' mark values that are provisional until the lab pilot. Revised 2026-10-04 for the online build (decisions 85-124 of the Uncertainty session 20261004T012954Z-claude-numerosity-interview-instructions-d0471d; its playable demo is the specification of the screens and their wording): the ring, the number line above the centre with the OK button at the centre, the block multiplier and the square-root payment, the instruction slides, the text screens and every participant string. The practice study (exp0.json) is this file with its own id, run and pay. Author 2026-10-18: the stacked betting response (betting_stack: 20 betting tokens on bins of 3 counts on the axis layout's betting space, poured, 4000 ms (5000 ms until the author's follow-up the same day), the share of tokens on the true count's bin x 100 points, nothing for a true count outside the betting space) replaces the betting range in the range's place, and the pre-cue is drawn per trial from 500-800 ms (timing.fixation_jitter_ms); exp0.json (recruitment closed) keeps the betting range and the fixed pre-cue, so the two files no longer share their trial types, timing and wording. Revised the same day after the author played the build: one bin per count, the drag control, no confirmation (the coins on the line at the window's end are the response), coins in the wording, the stack's example trial without a time limit, no correct answer on the estimation try.

display._note: One uniform mid-grey for every screen, so the eye is adapted to the same luminance throughout. sRGB 176 is ~2x the linear luminance of sRGB 128, and 0 is black, so dark and bright dots/checks balance around the background in linear light (nominal, uncalibrated monitor).

sizing._note: Author, 2026-10-14: no viewing distance and no visual angle. One reference layout at 1920 x 1080 physical pixels, scaled uniformly by s = min(W / 1920, H / 1080), W x H the full-screen window's physical (backing-store) pixels, so the operating system's display scaling and the browser zoom change nothing on the screen (2560 x 1440: s = 1.33; 3840 x 2160: 2; 2880 x 1800: 1.5, its width deciding; 2560 x 1080: 1). A degree of this file is reference_px_per_deg reference pixels: 44.3, the median of the 21 recorded Exp1 runs at their card-measured scale (physical px per degree), so at s = 1 the dot field of 5.4 deg is about 239 px, a dot of 0.32 deg about 14.2 px across, the scaling arc of 7.5 deg about 332 px in radius; the number line is spaces.count.length_reference_px. Every online run's geometry is this layout (source pixel; src/core/units.ts).

cloud._note: DeWind et al. (2015) size/spacing scheme. For a count N, log Size (= log item area + log total area) and log Spacing (= log field area + log sparsity) are drawn independently of N, so N is uncorrelated with Size, Spacing and coverage. Item area, field area, total area and density then necessarily co-vary with N and are recorded as covariates.

fixation._note: The combined bullseye and cross-hair target of Thaler et al. (2013). Shown during the inter-trial interval in `srgb` (black); during the pre-cue (timing.fixation_ms) it keeps its size and takes `pre_stimulus_srgb` (author, 2026-10-02: colour only, no size change), so its change of colour is the fixed warning before the cloud; removed at cloud onset. After a miss it is shown once in missing_response.missing_rgb (the yellow mark). Author, 2026-10-16: sized for stable fixation as in Thaler, Schuetz, Goodale and Gegenfurtner (2013, Vision Research 76, 31-42), the bullseye with the cross hair: an outer disc of 0.6 deg, the cross hair in the background colour, an inner disc of 0.2 deg, the cross hair as wide as the inner disc (0.2 deg); in pixels from an assumed typical setup of about 40 px per degree at the 1920 x 1080 reference (about 60 cm from a 24-inch monitor): outer 24 px, inner and cross hair 8 px, written here in this file's degrees (display.sizing: 44.3 reference px each): 24 / 44.3 = 0.5418 and 8 / 44.3 = 0.1806, so the pixel sizing rule scales them like every other size. The same mark on every screen that draws it (interval, pre-cue in pre_stimulus_srgb, estimation, betting, practice feedback, yellow mark after a miss).

set._status: read by build stage 1 (fixed stimulus set, 2026-10-01); files built by tools/build_stimulus_set.ts and tools/build_schedules.ts; hashes are raw-byte SHA-256 recomputed by the loader

timing._note: Prospective 2026-10-06 shared target timing: exact exposures of 5 and 18 frames (60 Hz reference 83.333/300 ms), changed 2026-10-17 (author, meeting decision) to 5 and 30 frames (60 Hz reference 83.333/500 ms) because 83 vs 300 ms did not separate the uncertainty conditions enough (Exp0 keeps its own timing), 750 ms white precue, and a contiguous 250 ms static pixel-noise mask. Betting lasts 3500 ms in every block (until 2026-10-18; since then the stacked betting response lasts 4000 ms in every block; author 2026-10-18, first 5000 ms, then 4000 ms). Author 2026-10-18: the white pre-cue's total length is drawn per trial, uniformly from fixation_jitter_ms [500, 800] ms (fixation_ms stays the fallback); the fixed trial length counts the longest, 800 ms. Author 2026-10-19 (wave 12): fixation_jitter_ms [300, 700] ms, so the fixed trial length counts 700 ms. The fixed slot uses the measured refresh interval for frame-count conditions. Each experiment retains its own feedback duration and reward rules. Mask appearance remains provisional pending author approval.
timing._allowed_refresh_hz_note: Author 2026-10-19: displays of 60, 120 or 144 Hz are admitted (the Prolific profile's refresh.expected_hz, within 2 Hz; any other rate is refused). exposure_frames are counted at 60 Hz and scaled to the nominal rate: 83.33 ms = 5, 10 or 12 frames and 500 ms = 30, 60 or 72 frames. The interval, the pre-cue, the mask and the feedback stay in ms, rounded to frames at the measured rate; the fixed trial length differs between the rates by at most the pre-cue's rounding (800 ms = 115 frames = 798.6 ms at 144 Hz). The session file records the nominal rate and the frames (environment.refresh_nominal_hz, exposure_frames).

feature_assignment._note: Wave 12 (author, 2026-10-19; generator schedule-2.0.0, config/design/stimulus_set/schedules_balanced.json): Size and Spacing are each split into thirds of their log range. Six main blocks: every (level x exposure) cell once per block; over the six blocks a cell shows six different images, each size third twice and each spacing third twice; in every block each image appears 3 or 4 times, each third 10 times, and a level's two cells show different images. The order of the main blocks is permuted per participant. The practice (train set): practice A, B and C of 10 trials (together every cell once; each part one short and one long cell of every band of three consecutive levels) and practice blocks 1 and 2 of every cell; a level's six practice trials show six different images, each third twice. Until wave 11 the Latin-thirds design of nine test blocks (config/design/stimulus_set/schedules.json, kept for exp0.json).

spaces._note: The two response widgets (author, 2026-10-03, decisions 76-78). count = the number line of the estimation response and the betting range (absolute space, values are counts): a horizontal line 3 degrees above the screen centre (y_offset_deg -3, no random shift), length_reference_px reference pixels long (2026-10-14: 1056 = 0.55 x 1920, so the line of 1920 x 1080 on every window of at least that size, a wide 2560 x 1080 one too; before, length_fraction_of_width 0.55 of the stage width, Exp1 revision 2), 8 to 76 so that its middle is 42 (the mirror centre of the two contexts), no ticks and no labels; the estimation response is snapped to an integer (point_snap) and the betting ends too (interval_snap); probe_number writes the integer under the cursor above the preview disc on the named phases only (the estimation screen; the betting screen shows no number). rho = the scaling arc of the scaling response (relative space, values in [0, 1]): a half circle of radius_deg around the screen centre, always centred there, whose orientation (the angle of its middle) is drawn per trial from the trial seed and recorded, 'Smaller' and 'Larger' at its ends (end_labels), values growing from the 'Smaller' end to the 'Larger' end in `direction`. A line is shape 'line' (length, height, shift); an arc is shape 'arc' (radius, span, orientation, direction); a key of the other shape is refused. The scaling arc and the number line differ in shape so that a screen position cannot be copied from one to the other. Revised 2026-10-04: the number line lies 3 deg above the screen centre (y_offset_deg -3, decision 96), so the betting button sits on the fixation mark's place; the scaling arc is drawn as a ring (spaces.rho.ring, decisions 92 and 123: a 1-deg band over the whole circle, the response half black (author, 2026-10-14; a blue-to-red gradient from Smaller to Larger before), the other half grey 112, radial bars inside the band for the probe, the highlight, the participant's answer and the green true position); its orientation is drawn over the upper half only, [-90, 90] in the convention 0 = straight up, clockwise positive (decision 89).

axis_layout._note: Author, 2026-10-16 (second version of the typed estimate): per trial an axis direction from the screen centre (0 right, 90 up, 180 left, 270 down; never drawn), balanced within each block; the typed entry box centred 200 reference px along it; after Enter the typed number disappears and the betting space opens through its place, perpendicular to the axis (horizontal for 90 and 270, vertical for 0 and 180), estimate - 12 to estimate + 12 counts at 31 reference px a count (744 px), more dots to the right or upwards, cut at 1; a larger mark at the estimate's place, small unlabelled marks every 5 counts from it, marks at the two ends, nothing else; the count under the cursor written small next to the probe while it is on the space (hover_number; reverses the 2026-10-03 rule of no numbers on the betting screen); no OK button: the live points number is a round button 380 reference px along the axis (fixation mark, estimate, button on one line), inactive until both ends are set, a press on it confirms. Practice feedback: the typed number at its place, the correct count in a green label beside it on the centre's side (at least the size of the typed digits), the green disc of the correct count or an arrow at the space's end beyond +-12, the points at the button's place. Every text container is sized from its text (text_padding_deg). The marks, fonts, button size and the walkthrough and stills axes are provisional. Revised the same day (author, 2026-10-16: "실제 정답 숫자 보여주지 말고 넘버라인에 위치만 정답시 초록, 오답시 빨강으로 표시. 얻은 보상점수와 헷갈려서 내린 결정. 만약 24 betting bound 바깥에 정답이 있다면, betting bound 바깥쪽에 1칸 떨어진 위치에 표시."): feedback_correct - the correct count is never written; its disc is green (true_position_rgb) when the betting range contains it and red (response_display.true_position_miss_rgb) when it does not; a correct count beyond the space is marked by the same disc 1 count beyond the end on its side (estimate + 13 or estimate - 13), no arrow. The typed number stays at its place and the points at the button's place. Remove feedback_correct for the first version (the green label, the arrow). The estimation walkthrough of the instructions places its green disc by the same beyond_end_counts. Author 2026-10-18 (second play-test of the stacked betting coins): up and down only (directions_deg [90, 270]), still balanced within each block.

trial_types._note: Named trial phase lists (author decision 1.5 and the review of 2026-10-02): the blocks section names the trial type each block runs. Every list starts with the stimulus phase; response phases follow; a feedback phase may follow any response phase and runs only in the block types it names (train; test trials carry no feedback time, decision 63). Feedback (author, 2026-10-02 evening): one feedback screen right after the betting range (the number line with the estimation disc, the range bar, the true count's position in green and the range points) and one after the scaling response (the scaling arc with the scaling disc, the true percentile's position in green, the scaling points and the total); each screen shows the responses made since the previous feedback. Each rewarded phase is paid by its own rule against the target of its own space. Response windows in Exp1 revision 2: estimation and scaling 2.5 s, betting 3.5 s; each exercise feedback screen 1.5 s. cursor_start (decisions 4, 79): the cursor is placed at the screen centre on the estimation and scaling screens and continues from the estimation click on the betting screen. The betting range (interval phase, method two_clicks_and_button): the participant clicks the two ends on the number line, then the round betting button below the line; until the button is pressed a new click on the line starts a new range whose other end must be clicked again; the window's end without the button is a miss; with must_contain_anchor a confirmed range that leaves out the estimation response is a miss (author, 2026-10-02). A miss (any response window that ends without a response, or a range that leaves out the estimation response) ends the trial's responses, voids every reward of the trial and deducts reward.miss_penalty_points; the fixation mark turns yellow once for missing_response.mark_ms, then the black mark follows until the next pre-cue; no later response phase and no feedback screen of the trial runs (author, 2026-10-03, decisions 53, 54, 63). Revised 2026-10-04: the betting button is a 2.2-deg disc with the word OK (text.betting_button) at [0, 3] deg from the middle of the number line, i.e. at the screen centre where the fixation mark is (decisions 94, 96); the range feedback writes the range points large at the centre with the word 'points' (show.points_large, decision 103); the scaling feedback shows only the green bar, no points and no total (decisions 119, 121: the scaling response earns no points of its own; its block's errors set the block multiplier). Revised 2026-10-16 (author: "대안 1로 우선 실험 제작 후 진화", a first version to be iterated; second version the same day): the estimation response is typed (entry: digits of the top row or the numeric pad, Backspace, at most 2 digits, Enter confirms an entry of at least 1; the 2.5 s window and the miss rule unchanged), its box on the trial's axis, and the betting range is set on the axis layout's betting space (spaces.count.axis_layout) with the round points button in place of OK; the betting cursor starts at the estimate's place (cursor_start anchor). Exp0 and the line mode keep the click on the line (remove entry and spaces.count.axis_layout, cursor_start continue). Author 2026-10-18: the stacked betting response replaces the betting range in the range's place (full: stimulus, estimation, betting_stack, feedback_stack, scaling, feedback_scaling; estimation_betting: stimulus, estimation, betting_stack, feedback_stack). The stack (src/trial/phases/stack.ts): 20 betting tokens on bins of 3 counts of the axis layout's betting space around the estimate (estimate +- 12 counts); a press places one token at once and, with the button still held 250 ms after it, tokens keep coming at 8 a second where the cursor is (control click_hold, author 2026-10-18; the first version poured from the press); a right click or Backspace takes the top token off; the response is confirmed when the last token lands, within 4000 ms (author 2026-10-18; 5000 ms in the first version of that day); a stack not finished in time is a missed response (the one miss rule above). Reward height_power with exponent 1: the share of the 20 tokens on the true count's bin x 100 points; tokens elsewhere earn nothing, and a true count outside the betting space (estimate +- 12) earns nothing even inside an end bin that overlaps the space (author 2026-10-18; src/trial/stack.ts scoringBin). Its practice feedback marks such a count as the range's feedback does, by the red disc 1 count beyond the end, and marks no bin. The tokens are drawn as red casino chips seen slightly from the side (draw.chip, author 2026-10-18); on the practice feedback after points, gold coins fly from the winning stack into the points number, which counts up (show.coins, coins_ms 1000; false switches it off). Its practice feedback feedback_stack marks the true count's bin with its tokens and writes the points large. The sentences above about the betting range describe the design before 2026-10-18 (and exp0.json). Author 2026-10-18, after playing the build (this supersedes the control, confirmation and bins above): one bin per count (bin_counts 1, 25 bins over estimate +- 12); control drag (a press drops one coin on the bin under the cursor; while held, each new bin entered gets one coin at once, so a sweep lays a row; resting on a bin adds coins at 8 a second after 250 ms); no confirmation (confirm none, on_timeout confirm_partial): the coins on the line when the 4000 ms window ends are the response, unplaced coins count for nothing, and a response with no coin is a missed response; the estimate and estimate +- 10 written along the space (spaces.count.axis_layout.labels); participant wording says coins. Second play-test of the same day: the coins must include the estimate (must_contain_anchor: a response without a coin on the estimate's bin is a missed response, missing_reason excludes_anchor, as the old range's must_contain_anchor; the yellow mark's line text.feedback_excludes_anchor in practice blocks); no bar on the line under the cursor or the piles; axes up and down only (spaces.count.axis_layout.directions_deg [90, 270]). Author 2026-10-19 (wave 12; this supersedes the 20 coins, the 8 a second and the excludes-anchor miss above): 25 coins (tokens), the first standing on the participant's own estimate bin when the screen opens (preplaced_on_anchor: drawn and paid as any coin, the counter starts at 24 / 25 left, a right click or Backspace on that bin removes only the coins placed above it, recorded apart as the event how preplaced and the outcome's preplaced); a stack with no coin of the participant's own besides it is a missed response (proposal of the build, 2026-10-20); must_contain_anchor false (the pre-placed coin always holds the estimate, so the excludes-anchor miss cannot occur); holding pours 8 a second from 250 ms, then 10 a second after 500 ms of pouring on the same press or rest (pour_accel_after_ms, pour_max_rate_per_s). Practice A (trial type estimation): the stimulus, the typed estimation as in full, then feedback_estimation (practice only, 1500 ms): the estimation screen's place on the trial's axis with the typed estimate written there, the betting space's line through it and the correct count's green disc on that line (beyond_end_counts past the end when it lies off the space), as the estimation walkthrough shows it; a missed estimate shows the yellow mark as every miss does.

reward._status: Author 2026-10-06: base £7 per completed session, maximum total £12, target median total £9.5. The target is not an observed or guaranteed payment. Existing point anchors and square-root conversion retained pending N=10 Exp0 sanity check.

range._note: Author 2026-10-15: the range rule hit_exponential (100 points up to 6 counts, falling ten-fold by 24, floor 10) replaced by hit_power: on a hit, 100 points up to 3 counts, 100 * (L / 3)^(-0.6) up to 24, 0 beyond; a range that misses the count earns 0 (the missed-response deduction is unchanged). Why: under the exponential rule the best range length stays near 7 counts whatever the uncertainty; a power law has no length scale, so the best length grows with the uncertainty. No penalties, by the advisor's view relayed by the author. Exp0 and the Exp1 sessions recorded before this change keep hit_exponential in their config snapshots.

payment._note_2026_10_06_raise: Author 2026-10-06: the Exp1 base raised to 8 pounds before its recruitment (sessions ran longer than designed and Betting performance was low); the bonus range of 5 pounds is unchanged.
payment._note_2026_10_12_refit: Author 2026-10-12: the anchors refit (anchor_none_per_trial 10.5 -> 5, anchor_best_per_trial 145.9 -> 103; conversion square_root, base 8, max 13 and target_median 9.5 unchanged) to the 14 recorded sessions of the 7 people who pass the practice screen (blocks.practice_screen): points per main trial median 13.8, range 3.8-25.7; median total 9.50 pounds. With the practice screen in Session 1, a Session 1 bonus of 0 now means no Session 2. New runs only: a session file pays by the anchors of its own config_snapshot.
payment._note_2026_10_15_rule: Author 2026-10-15: the range rule changed to hit_power (reward.range). anchor_none_per_trial and anchor_best_per_trial were fit to sessions paid by hit_exponential and must be refit for the new range rule; the refit is pending the author's decision. No pay value changed here.
payment._note_2026_10_19_pay: Author 2026-10-19: base 8 -> 7, max 13 (bonus up to 6), square_root unchanged; anchors refit by Fable for the betting-coins rule (anchor_none_per_trial 5 -> 1.5, anchor_best_per_trial 103 -> 12 points per main trial). Fable's realistic careful participant totals about 9.0-9.8 pounds, so target_median stays 9.5 (the slide's typical total).

stop_pay._note_wave_12: Author 2026-10-19 (wave 12): either screening ends the session with practice_screen, 1 pound (no graded amount); the repeated-value stop (stopped.reason repeated_value) pays nothing. The stop screen names the run's own amount ({practice_pay} from the file's payment).
stop_pay._note: Author 2026-10-19: early-stop pay by reason, without the hourly floors (6 and 9 pounds per hour no longer apply). A stop by the practice checks (stopped.reason practice_screen: a failed check, or No twice to a practice question) is paid practice_screen; the 90-minute session limit (time_limit) the base only, no bonus; a page error the larger of error_minimum and base x completed blocks / blocks of the run (not the participant's fault; the author's rule is pending, see docs/DECISIONS.md); every other stop (the stop rule's misses, the second departure, a too-long absence) nothing. A device refusal is never a run and is never paid.

missing_response._note: One miss rule (author, 2026-10-02): a miss is a response window that ends without a response (estimation, range or scaling) or a confirmed range that leaves out the estimation response. What follows (author, 2026-10-03, decisions 53, 54, 74): the fixation mark (the bullseye and cross) is shown in missing_rgb, alone on the background, once, for mark_ms; then the ordinary black mark follows until the next trial's pre-cue at its fixed time. No later response phase and no feedback screen of the trial runs; the trial's rewards are void and reward.miss_penalty_points is deducted. In the block types of deduction_in_block_types (train) the deducted points are written beside the yellow mark (text.feedback_miss, in response_display.points_negative_rgb) for the same mark_ms. When the yellow mark runs past the missed slot (mark_ms is longer than response_display.highlight_ms), the black interval before the next pre-cue may shorten to min_interval_after_mark_ms so the cloud keeps its time; the loader requires mark_ms <= highlight_ms + timing.iti_ms - min_interval_after_mark_ms. Author 2026-10-19 (wave 12): the deduction is reward.miss_penalty_points 20 (from 50); a stack that leaves out the estimate is no longer a miss (the coin pre-placed on the estimate's bin), so excludes_anchor_note is not reached from this file.

excludes_anchor_note._note: Author, 2026-10-05: after a range that leaves out the estimate, in the exercise blocks only, text.feedback_excludes_anchor is written under the yellow mark for the same mark_ms (no change to timing). A participant had finished the walkthrough correctly but 29 of 49 exercise ranges excluded their estimate.

response_display._note: Appearance and input rules shared by the response screens. Lengths in degrees of visual angle; colours are sRGB grey levels unless an [r, g, b] triple. Markers are discs (marker_diameter_deg); the betting range is a bar of range_bar_width_deg on the line with a disc at each end; a faint preview disc (preview_srgb) shows where a click would land, only within the click band of the widget (preview_in_band_only, decision 78); after a response its mark (or the range) brightens to highlight_srgb for highlight_ms before the next screen (author, 2026-10-03, decision 61: 0.3 s). The cursor: the real pointer is hidden with the pointer lock and a drawn cursor (cursor.*) follows the mouse; each response phase's cursor_start places it (centre: the screen centre; continue: where the previous response screen left it; random: a seeded position inside the stage margins, cursor.margin_deg), recorded; without the lock the real pointer is used and the record says so. On a screen whose cursor starts at the centre nothing marks a value and no click is taken until the cursor is reveal_after_move_deg from its start (decision 78). input_lockout_ms: presses during this time after a response screen appears are ignored and counted. Every points number - the live number of the betting screen, the feedback lines and the deduction beside the yellow mark - is coloured by its sign: above 0 in points_positive_rgb (green), below 0 in points_negative_rgb (red), 0 in the text grey (author, 2026-10-02 evening). After the visual review of 2026-10-04 (orchestrator's fix, provisional until the author sees it): every coloured element - each coloured points number and the true-position marker - is drawn over a thin outline in outline_srgb, outline_width_deg beyond its edge (the green and the red have about 1.3:1 luminance contrast against the grey of sRGB 128, the black outline about 5.3:1; the hues are unchanged). The true-position marker lies in its own lane: a green disc true_position_offset_deg from the widget (above the number line; inside the scaling arc, true_position_arc_side) joined to the exact true position on the widget by a green tick true_position_tick_width_deg wide, so the disc never covers the participant's marks. Revised 2026-10-04: the live points number under the OK button is 3.0 deg tall to match the large reward feedback (Exp1 revision 2); the fixation mark is drawn on the estimation and scaling screens (decision 96); the large feedback points are 3 deg tall at the centre with the word 'points' under them (decision 103). The ring ignored around the betting button is 0.3 deg (0.5 before 2026-10-04): with the button at the centre, 3 deg below the line, its top then lies 1.6 deg below the line, outside the 1.5-deg click band (checked by the loader). Added 2026-10-16 (author): true_position_miss_rgb, the red of the correct count's disc on the practice range feedback when the betting range leaves it out (spaces.count.axis_layout.feedback_correct.colour_by_hit), the same red as points_negative_rgb and the [red] label of the slides (#ff4a3d), drawn over the dark red outline (outline_rgb.negative_rgb) so it reads on the grey; provisional.

cursor._note_2026_10_14: Author, 2026-10-14: the pointer lock is asked for with raw movement (unadjustedMovement), the ordinary lock when the browser refuses it, and which was granted is recorded; the cursor moves reference_px_per_count x s physical px per unit of movement, so the number line (1056 reference px) spans about 1056 mouse counts and the scaling arc's half circle (pi x 7.5 x 44.3 = 1044 reference px) about 1044 at every window size. Sub-frame samples (getCoalescedEvents) of every response window are kept delta-encoded (samples; pointer_samples of the outcome).

text._note: Participant wording revised 2026-10-06: Estimate, Choose a range, and Compare. Compare asks about other pictures with fewer dots relative to the pattern shown at the start; the target remains the reference CDF, not the empirical rank of displayed trials. Identifiers and recorded field names are unchanged. Text outside this section is research/operator metadata, not participant copy.

body.text: On each trial, **dots** appear briefly. You then answer about **how many** there were.
[pill]{n_exercise_blocks} practice blocks[/pill] and [pill]{n_main_blocks} main blocks[/pill]; a main block takes about {block_minutes} minutes.
Task time: at least about {task_minutes} minutes, set by the structure of the task.
Instructions, short questions and breaks come on top. We recommend a break of 5 seconds to 1 minute between blocks.

Later in the session, a screen tells you when the time limit of {limit_minutes} minutes starts. If the time runs out, the session ends there and you receive the base payment of {currency}{base}, without a bonus.

center.title: Keep your eyes on the center

body.text: The center mark turns **white** just before the dots appear.
Answering faster does not shorten the session.
A missed or invalid answer ends the trial. That trial earns no points and costs [red]−{miss_points}[/red]; the center mark turns [yellow]yellow[/yellow].
In session 1, after some practice blocks, you are asked whether the task is clear.
Your practice answers are also checked. If the session cannot go on to the main blocks, it ends there and you receive {currency}{practice_pay}.
The dots appear only briefly. Estimate roughly how many you saw, at a glance.
Type your **estimate** on the keyboard and press [pill]Enter[/pill] within [pill]{estimation_s} s[/pill].
Type the exact number you estimate; do not round it.
Entering the same number again and again can end the session without payment.
Type your **estimate** of the number of dots on the keyboard and press [pill]Enter[/pill] within [pill]{estimation_s} s[/pill].
Place your **betting range** on the numbers where you expect to win points: click its two ends, then click the button with the points. The range must include your estimate.
The line goes through your estimate, with a small mark every 5. Further right or higher means more dots.
Use two separate clicks, one at each end, not a double click.
If the correct answer falls inside your betting range, it wins points: the narrower the range, the more points, up to [green]{range_max_points}[/green]. The number on the button shows them.
Adjust your betting range to how sure you are of the number, so that you earn as many points as possible.
In practice blocks, the place of the [green]correct answer[/green] is shown on the line: [green]green[/green] when it is inside your betting range, [red]red[/red] when it is not.
Practice points are not paid.
Place up to {stack_tokens} **betting coins** on the line where you think the number is.
Each coin on the correct number earns [green]{stack_token_points}[/green] points; coins elsewhere earn nothing.
The middle of the line is your estimate. Your coins must include it.
Click to place a coin; hold and drag to place a row of coins. A right click removes the top coin from a pile.
On every trial, place your coins to reflect how sure you are, so that you earn as many points as you can.
Your coins count when the time is up ([pill]{stack_s} s[/pill]).
In practice blocks, the [green]correct answer[/green] is marked on the line, with the points your coins earned there.
Practice points are not paid.
Each trial also asks for a **relative estimate**: where the number you saw stands in this session's distribution, as a **percentile** from 0 % to 100 %.

rows: the smallest number in the distribution
about the middle: half of the distribution is smaller

body.text: In the picture, the number you saw (arrow) is larger than about 30 % of the distribution (the dark area), so its relative estimate is about **30 %**.
Click your relative estimate on the black half of the ring, the **arc**.
The example is at about 30 %.
The arc's position on the ring changes from trial to trial, so check its end words each time.
Relative estimates do not earn points trial by trial.

At the end of each block, their accuracy over the whole block sets **one factor**: [green]×{max_factor}[/green] when they are close to the correct answers, down to [pill]×{min_factor}[/pill] when they are far off.
The block's total betting points are multiplied by this factor once.
From now on, each trial has all three steps:
[pill]Absolute estimate[/pill] → [pill]Betting coins[/pill] → [pill]Relative estimate[/pill]
Main blocks are like the last practice block, but the correct answer is not shown.
The more points, the bigger the bonus.
We aim for a typical total payment of {currency}{target_median}. Your total depends on your performance.
If you miss [pill]{stop_misses}[/pill] answers in one main block, the session ends early.
No payment is made in that case.

blocks._note: The blocks of a session (decision 1.5): the train blocks first in their stored order, then the test blocks in the participant's seeded order (src/design/order.ts), 30 trials each. A block names the trial type its trials run directly: entry k of train_trial_types is the trial type of stored train block k (so the list has one entry per train block of every context's schedule; the loader checks it), and every test block runs test_trial_type. A run is what the experiment page shows in one sitting: session = the whole session (all train blocks, all test blocks); pilot = the three train blocks and the first test block of the participant's order (author, 2026-10-02 evening: every block kind of the session is tried in the pilot). train_block_indices are stored train block indices and run in stored order; n_test_blocks keeps the first that many test blocks of the order. The intro screen before each block shows the picture of the session context's count distribution (show_distribution, distribution_picture; decision 64) and its Start button becomes active after intro_min_ms; after Start the first trial's black interval lasts lead_in_ms (decision 75). The block clock (align_trials; decisions 56, 62): every trial's pre-cue has a fixed target, the block origin + k x the fixed trial length + timing.iti_ms, so all unused time goes to the next inter-trial interval and every cloud comes at its fixed time; a lateness above clock_reset_after_ms re-sets the origin at that trial, a smaller one is recovered in the next interval. Between blocks the rest screen's button becomes active after rest_min_ms (author, 2026-09-30: at least 5 s). block_total = the rest screen shows the points of the block just finished and the end screen the paid total and its conversion; test blocks show no feedback after a trial, only this total. stop_rule (author, 2026-10-03, decision 84): in a block of block_kinds, the trial that brings the block's misses to max_misses ends the block and the run at once (after its yellow mark); no later trial or block runs, the stop screen (text.screen_stopped) shows, and the record is saved and downloaded as at a normal end, with status stopped; the run is paid reward.payment.base x the blocks completed before the stopping block / the blocks of the run, without a bonus; null = no stop. Revised 2026-10-04: the instruction slides are placed by the instructions section; block screens name the kinds Exercise and Main block (decision 118). Wave 12 (author, 2026-10-19): the session follows blocks.sequence: practice A (trial type estimation, 10 trials), practice B (estimation_betting, 10), practice C (scaling, 10), practice block 1 (full, 30, feedback), three main blocks, practice block 2 (full, 30, feedback), three main blocks; 270 trials, 180 of them in main blocks; the main blocks are the participant's order of the six stored test blocks. The learning phase (the learning section) comes before practice A, the time-limit warning (session.limit_start) before practice block 1. The pilot run: practice A, B, C, practice block 1 and the first main block.
blocks._lock_wait_ms_note: 2026-10-12: a Start press waits at most this long for the browser to grant or refuse the pointer lock; no answer counts as a refused request (lock_attempts), and a lock granted later is released. Before this key a browser that answered neither way left the Start button disabled.
blocks._betting_check_note: Wave 12 (2026-10-20): the practice-B coin check is off (null), so it never repeats practice B or ends the run; screening 1's missed-response rule (practice_checks, answered_per_step) covers practice B. Until wave 11: trial_type estimation_betting, phase betting_stack, min_missed_fraction 0.5, max_repeats 1, slide_group guess_stack.

practice_checks._note: Wave 12 (author, 2026-10-19; supersedes the checks after each practice block of 2026-10-14): Session 1 only, two screenings, no retry; Session 2 runs the same parts with no question and no check. Block positions count from 0 (practice A 0, B 1, C 2, practice block 1 3). Screening 1 after practice C: the question text.practice_question.questions.full (Yes or No; max_repeats 0, so No ends the session), then answered_per_step over practice A, B and C: for every block and every response step of its trials (A: the estimate; B: the estimate and the betting coins; C: the relative estimate) the answered responses out of the block's trials; the session ends if any step has fewer than min (proposal: 4 of 10). Screening 2 after practice block 1: estimation_error (the mean |estimate - N| in dots over the answered estimates; N = cell.level) above 12 in context S or 15 in context L, or scaling_rank_correlation (Spearman, average ranks for ties, 0 when a variable is constant) between the relative estimate and the true percentile cell.rho below 0.70, or fewer than min_answered (10) answered, ends the session. Every ending: stopped.reason practice_screen, practice_checks.ended_by.screening screening_1 or screening_2 (every step carries its screening), at the next block, the early-stop completion code, paid reward.payment.stop_pay.practice_screen (1 pound); text.stop.practice_lines after a check, text.stop.practice_question_lines after a No. A check run (trials_per_block) records the checks without stopping unless its address asks (enforce_checks=1).

estimate_warnings._note: Wave 12 (author, 2026-10-19; src/session/estimate_checks.ts). rounding (proposal): after practice A, B and practice block 1, when more than half of the part's answered estimates are divisible by 10, the screen text.estimate_warnings.rounding before the next part; no stop (the exclusion threshold is the author's, at review). repeated_value: after a main block in which one estimate value makes up more than half of the answered estimates, the screen text.estimate_warnings.repeated_value before the next block; the next main block that does so ends the run at once (stopped.reason repeated_value, at the next block, no payment: reward.payment.stop_pay.repeated_value 0, the early-stop completion code, text.stop.repeated_value_lines; the participant goes to the exclusion group at review). Every warning and stop is in the session file's estimate_warnings; the earlier main blocks are judged again from the file's rows, so a resumed run counts the same. A check run shows the warning in place of the stop unless its address asks (enforce_checks=1).

Wave 12 (author, 2026-10-19): the absolute estimate slide (and its try) is its own group, estimation, before practice A (trial type estimation); the coin slides (guess_stack: stack, its example, feedback) before practice B; the ring slides and the check before practice C; the all-three slide before practice block 1; the distribution slide stays in the session start's group, before the learning phase.

session._status: Wave 12 (2026-10-20): estimated_minutes and listed_minutes are placeholders until the build's step 4 (the listed time = the minimum task time without breaks plus the median, author 2026-10-19); the welcome slide's task time ({task_minutes}) comes from the plan (sum of block.fixed_trial_ms * block.n_trials) and the learning phase's clouds. Before wave 12: 2026-10-18 (the stacked betting response and the pre-cue drawn per trial, author 2026-10-18): pure scheduled task time at 60 Hz is 4113 seconds (68 min 33 s), sum(block.fixed_trial_ms * block.n_trials) for one full session (360 trials): the stack's 4000 ms window adds 500 ms to each of the 330 trials with a betting response (the range had 3500 ms), and the fixed trial length counts the longest pre-cue, 800 ms of timing.fixation_jitter_ms [500, 800] (50 ms more than the fixed 750 ms; the shorter draws lengthen the next black interval, not the session), so 183 s more than the 3930 seconds of the long exposure 500 ms (author 2026-10-17; 3858 seconds on 2026-10-06 with 300 ms). Both minute fields round this up (66 -> 69; 75 with the stack's first window of 5000 ms). Excludes setup, instructions, block introductions, lead-in correction, breaks, repeats, and final survey; does not promise wall-clock completion time. The Prolific study files (ops/prolific/config/studies/exp1_s1.json, exp1_s2.json) still list 65 minutes and their pay: to be changed with the author's pay decision before the next Exp1 study.
session._limit_minutes_note: Wave 12 (author, 2026-10-19): a warning before practice block 1 (text.time_limit_warning, session.limit_start), then 60 minutes from its button; reaching them ends the run where it is (stopped.reason time_limit), paid the base without a bonus, with the time-limit completion code; a return after it ends the same way. Until the warning the run has no session limit. Until wave 11: 90 minutes from consent. Author 2026-10-19: the whole online session ends 90 minutes after consent wherever it is (stopped.reason time_limit), paid the base without a bonus, with its own completion code (time_limit of the study files); a return after it ends the same way. Replaces online.resume.session_factor x listed_minutes (138 minutes) for Exp1. Rest screens stay unlimited within it. Stated once on the welcome slide and in the Prolific description.

The learning phase sets are built by tools/build_stimulus_set.ts (npm run set:build: the same generator, sizes, spacings and thirds as the test and train sets, their own set ids so their own seeds) and checked by analysis/check_stimulus_set.py; the loader recomputes the raw-byte SHA-256 below.
